Two years ago, Sonos expanded from wireless speakers into the over-ear headphone market. Now, it appears Sonos is preparing to launch a more positioned, higher-end successor product with artificial intelligence technology.

Sonos Ace Ultra over-ear headphones are about to debut

Chris Welch reports for Bloomberg that Sonos is developing the Sonos Ace Ultra, as an upgraded successor to the 2024 Ace headphones.

A US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) filing exposed on Monday mentions the product name and shows up to five color options, an increase from the original version's only black and white.

Sonos plans to hold a product launch event in September. Based on the filing's timeline, the Ace Ultra may be one of the products announced that day.

The filing also contains technical clues, indicating that the new headphones may support voice command functionality.

Bloomberg reports that CEO Tom Conrad acknowledged that the initial headphone launch lacked sufficient whole-home integration capabilities and also lacked clear differentiation in the highly competitive market for similar products.

This time, Sonos appears to intend to more directly integrate its hardware into a broader AI strategy.

Conrad has positioned the company's growth opportunities in conversational computing and predictive intelligence for the home environment, positioning Sonos devices as hardware that can operate across rooms and understand patterns of household life.

The company has expanded Sonos Voice Control to work with Philips Hue and Lutron Caseta.

Meanwhile, Apple's upgraded AirPods Max 2 launched in March, featuring the H2 chip, stronger noise cancellation, and real-time translation capabilities. Siri AI will extend to AirPods via iOS 27.

For details on the upcoming Sonos Ace Ultra over-ear headphones, refer to Bloomberg's full report.
